scenes.heading: Who runs what
scenes.sub: Four jobs, shared across your computers
scenes.say: Lampstand is built so a team can share the work of a Sunday service. Here is who runs what.

scenes.heading: A role is a job
items: A job someone is doing right now
Each job has one holder at a time
One computer can hold any mix of jobs
A computer with no job can still plan
scenes.say: A role is just a job that someone is doing right now. Each job has one holder at a time. One computer can hold any mix of jobs, and a computer with no job can still help plan the service.

scenes.heading: The four jobs
scenes.say: There are four jobs: Projection, Operator, Stream, and Audio.
Projection runs the screens. It is the picture on the projector and the stage screens. It lives on the computer that is plugged into them, and it can run on its own, with nobody sitting there.
Operator runs the service. Next, back, and jumping to any item. The Operator needs Projection to be running.
Stream runs what goes out online. That means OBS and the live stream. It keeps working even if the projector computer is away.
Audio runs the sound that Lampstand plays: videos, music, and backing tracks. It plays from the computer next to the mixer.

scenes.heading: One computer

machines.name: Your one laptop
machines.caption: Holds all four jobs. Nothing to set up.

scenes.say: With one computer, it holds all four jobs. There is nothing to set up.

scenes.heading: Two computers
scenes.say: With two computers, the one at the projector keeps Projection, Operator, and Audio, and the stream desk takes Stream.

scenes.heading: Three computers
scenes.say: With three, a laptop at the back of the room takes Operator, so someone can run the service from where they can see everything.

scenes.heading: Four computers
scenes.say: With four, the sound desk takes Audio, so music and videos play straight into the mixer.

scenes.caption: The same four computers, drawn out
scenes.say: Here is the same four-computer set-up, drawn out.

scenes.text: Phones and tablets can help, but they never hold a job.
scenes.say: Phones and tablets can help, for example as a remote, but they never hold a job.

scenes.heading: Handing a job over
items: Ask: press Take on the job you want
Allow: the holder sees Allow or Not now
Decline: choose Not now and nothing changes
Cut off: if the holder has been gone two minutes, anyone can take it
scenes.say: To hand a job over, one computer asks for it. The one holding it chooses Allow or Not now. And if the holder has been gone for two minutes, anyone can take it over.
Mary's laptop asks to take Stream. The holder sees the question, and chooses Allow. The job moves across.
If the holder chooses Not now, nothing changes. They keep the job.
If the holder is cut off, say the network drops, the job waits. After two minutes, Mary's laptop can take it over.

scenes.heading: What happens on screen
items: Operator passes: the slide stays up
Stream passes: OBS stays on its scene
scenes.say: When a job passes, Projection clears the screens, and Audio stops the music. Operator leaves the slide up, and Stream leaves OBS where it is.

scenes.text: A computer that comes back learns it lost the job, and does not grab it back.
scenes.say: A computer that comes back learns it lost the job, and does not grab it back.
